Readwise Reader charges $9.99/month and still caps how many questions you can ask its built-in AI before your next billing cycle resets.

Readwise Reader is the read-it-later app from the team behind Readwise's highlight-syncing tool. It pulls articles, PDFs, newsletters, RSS feeds, X/Twitter threads, YouTube transcripts, and EPUBs into one reading queue instead of scattering them across six tabs and three apps.

A few specifics worth knowing before you consider it:

→ $9.99/mo billed annually ($119.88/year) for the Full plan, which includes Reader. Month-to-month billing is $12.99/mo. A cheaper Lite tier ($5.59/mo) exists but drops Reader entirely — highlights only.
→ Ghostreader, the built-in AI, summarizes articles and answers questions about a document as you read it. Useful for deciding whether a long piece is worth your time, but it reads one document at a time — not a research tool across sources.
→ The interface is keyboard-first: vim-style j/k navigation through a three-pane layout, no mouse required.
→ Highlights feed into Readwise's spaced-repetition flashcard system, so something you highlighted in March can resurface as a review card in June.
→ Students and academics get 50% off any plan.

Worth flagging honestly: there's no permanent free tier after the 30-day trial, no team plans, and recent third-party reviews average 3.64/5, with people citing Ghostreader's credit caps and occasional lag as the main complaints.
